title: Nine States Elect History-Making Governors
summary:
On Tuesday, voters in nine states chose governors who made history.

In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms will be the first Black woman elected governor of any state. In New Mexico, Deb Haaland will be the first Native American woman governor in U.S. history.

California chose its first elected Latino governor, Xavier Becerra. Texas chose its first Latina governor, Gina Hinojosa — the first Democrat to win that job in Texas in more than 30 years.

Florida and Wisconsin elected their first Black governors: Byron Donalds in Florida and David Crowley in Wisconsin.

Three states elected a woman governor for the first time: Marsha Blackburn in Tennessee, Amy Klobuchar in Minnesota and Amy Acton in Ohio. Acton will also be Ohio's first Jewish governor.

Across the country, these races changed the picture of who can lead a state.
why_it_matters: Governors help run the state you live in, so who wins can change things like schools and roads near your home.
